title: How To Gain Control Of An Out-Of-Control Class https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2016/10/01/how-to-gain-control-of-an-out-of-control-class/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes an emergency, one-time strategy for the extreme scenario in which a teacher can't even get students' attention through waiting, and where anger and raised voices, while sometimes effective, carry a heavy relational cost. Called the "reciprocation strategy," it involves temporarily setting aside the classroom management plan and instead moving through the room engaging students individually with friendly, low-pressure remarks — commenting on shoes, asking how they're doing, thanking them for taking a seat — leveraging the deeply ingrained human tendency to return kindness with cooperation. As the teacher works back toward the front of the room while continuing to thank compliant students, they gradually regain enough control to launch immediately into reteaching rules and procedures as though it were the first day of school, since the cooperative window won't last. Linsin is explicit that this is a survival-mode, last-resort method, not something to rely on regularly, and that its purpose is solely to buy the few vital moments needed to restart the class.
points: The reciprocation strategy is a last-resort, emergency method for when a class has completely stopped responding to waiting.
It works by leveraging the human tendency to reciprocate kindness, using friendly, individual remarks while moving through the room.
The classroom management plan is temporarily set aside during the strategy in favor of low-pressure, personal engagement.
As soon as attention is regained, the teacher must immediately reteach rules and procedures as though it were the first day of school.
This is explicitly framed as a one-time, survival-mode method, not a strategy to rely on weekly or monthly.
quotes: After waiting in vain for several minutes, it’s only natural to get angry. With no other option, it’s only natural to threaten and raise your voice to try to reel them in.
The way it works is that the moment you realize that waiting isn't working, you're going to begin using what I call the reciprocation strategy.
You must appeal to the law of reciprocation, which states that if you're nice to someone, they'll want to be nice right back.
The friendlier and more easygoing you are, the better and faster the strategy will work.
At this point, however, it's critical to immediately dive into reteaching your rules, expectations, procedures, etc. as if it's the first day of school.

It isn’t a strategy you can rely on every week or even every month. It’s a one-time, survival-mode method to re-engage a class that you’ve lost and can’t get back without yelling, threatening, and driving a wedge through your relationship.
It gives you an opportunity, nothing more. So you must seize it. And never lose control again.
